questions.subject: Transformers
questions.question: Explain the difference between self-attention and positional encoding in Transformers.
questions.ideal_answer: self-attention and positional encoding differ in several ways: self-attention is intra-sequence attention (works by relating positions within sequence) whereas positional encoding is sequence order injection (works by adding position information). self-attention is typically used for Query, Key, Value matrices, softmax normalization, while positional encoding is used for sinusoidal or learned embeddings. Example demonstrating self-attention: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V. Example demonstrating positional encoding: PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model)).
